Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:

Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like late 2025. The fed funds rate is 3.87%, which fits after the cuts in September, October and December 2025; the effective rate was about 3.89% in December. Unemployment of 4.3% matches September 2025 data, and 4.4% was reported for October and November. Headline CPI of 3.02% is close to September 2025's 3.0%, and core CPI of 3.03% is close to the 3.0% reported for September.

The rate and CPI readings point to different months. A funds rate of 3.87% suggests after the October 2025 cut, when the effective rate was about 4.09% in October and 3.89% in November. Core CPI YoY was 3.0% in September, and the November print was 2.6%, which was distorted. The 3-month change in the funds rate of -0.46 fits November 2025 (August 4.33 to November 3.88). The 10-year yield of 4.11% in late November was about 4.02%, so that is roughly consistent.

Gold up 18.4% over 3 months fits end-November 2025, with gold moving from about 3400 to 4200. The 1-month gold gain of 3.8% fits November. US equities up 1.9% in 1 month fits November's roughly +0.2% less well, so October is also possible, but the funds rate points to November.

The payrolls 3-month average of 29k is weak, which suits data published through September, with delayed releases. Unemployment of 4.3% is the September figure, and the November release had not yet been published at the end of November. Core CPI of 3.03% is also the September figure. So the snapshot is probably November 2025.
